title: Assam: ATTSA protest enters seventh day over alleged tea factory safety lapses

ai.summary: A sit-in protest led by the Assam Tea Tribe Students’ Association (ATTSA) entered its seventh day in Talap Town, Assam, demanding stronger workplace safety measures after a worker died from machinery crushing at a tea factory.

facts.claim: A sit-in protest led by the Assam Tea Tribe Students’ Association (ATTSA) entered its seventh day in Talap Town, Assam
facts.quote: Doomdooma: A sit-in protest demanding stronger workplace safety measures in Assam’s tea factories entered its seventh day at Talap Town in Tinsukia district on Friday.

facts.claim: The protest follows the death of 42-year-old Ajay Gor, who was crushed by machinery while on duty at a factory belonging to Talup Tea Estate Company on November 20
facts.quote: The protest follows the death of 42-year-old Ajay Gor, who was crushed by machinery while on duty at a factory belonging to Talup Tea Estate Company on November 20.

facts.claim: The incident has renewed concerns over alleged safety lapses and the protection of workers in Assam’s tea industry
facts.quote: The incident has renewed concerns over alleged safety lapses and the protection of workers in Assam’s tea industry.

facts.claim: Lazar Nanda, vice-president of ATTSA’s central committee in Guwahati, criticised the factory management over the alleged lack of adequate safety arrangements
facts.quote: Addressing the protesters, Lazar Nanda, vice-president of ATTSA’s central committee in Guwahati, criticised the factory management over the alleged lack of adequate safety arrangements.

facts.claim: On November 2, 2023, the Chief Inspector of Factories, Assam, issued a notification directing all tea factories to appoint safety supervisors, constitute safety committees, provide personal protective equipment (PPE), install CCTV surveillance systems and follow proper safety procedures during machinery maintenance
facts.quote: On November 2, 2023, the Chief Inspector of Factories, Assam, issued a notification directing all tea factories to appoint safety supervisors, constitute safety committees, provide personal protective equipment (PPE), install CCTV surveillance systems and follow proper safety procedures during machinery maintenance.

facts.claim: The state government’s factory safety guidelines also place the responsibility on factory occupiers to protect workers’ health and safety through adequate equipment, training and supervision
facts.quote: The state government’s factory safety guidelines also place the responsibility on factory occupiers to protect workers’ health and safety through adequate equipment, training and supervision.

ai.background_note: The protest is part of ongoing concerns about workplace safety in Assam’s tea factories, following a worker’s death that has highlighted alleged safety lapses despite existing regulatory measures.
